newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Healthsource call volume jumps.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Healthsource call volume jumps.

text.p: Call volume in Healthsource Inc options rose notably this week, and traders said the increased call activity could suggest some investors knew of an impending buyout.
Healthsource rallied 4-3/8 to 20-7/8 on more than eight million shares after CIGNA Corp said Friday it agreed to buy Healthsource for $21.75 a share. The stock reached a session high of 21-3/8.
Traders said Friday that investors were mostly sellers of calls, which rose along with the stock.
But the traders were quick to point out that Healthsource also released earnings Friday, an event that often drives up options volume in advance.
A spokesman at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, where Healthsource options are listed, said a routine inquiry was open into trading in Healthsource options.
The spokesman said overall volume in Healthsource rose from 362 contracts on February 18 to 2,803 contracts on February 24. It declined to 1,552 on February 25 and to 529 on February 26.

One options strategist noted that turnover in the March 17-1/2 call in particular had increased dramatically over the last several days, reaching well over 1,000 Thursday, the day before the deal was announced.
He said volume Wednesday was about 270 in that contract.
The March 17-1/2 call rose two to 3-1/4 Friday on volume of 2,000 contracts. It reached a session high of four.
The contract had open interest of 2,080 contracts through Thursday, when 778 contracts were added.
One options trader said his firm was involved in the sale of a large block of the Healthsource March 17-1/2 calls Friday, adding that call selling was the main event.
Other active Healthsource calls included the March 15, which traded roughly 820 contracts, and the April 17-1/2, which traded about 825.
Open interest in the April 17-1/2 call rose 162 to 997 Thursday and in the March 15 call rose 32 to 886.
The October 17-1/2 call traded 420 options. Its open interest was 56, including an addition of 25 Thursday.
On the put side, the Healthsource March 20 was most active, with volume of 300 contracts.

The company reported a fourth quarter loss of $0.35 per share, which included a non-recurring charge of $0.40 a share. It earned a profit of $0.22 a share in the year-ago period. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
